variety: Cabécar, primarily the northern (Chirripó) dialect as used in the Bible.is New Testament (CJPTJV, the MMS-TTS training text) and Margery's d.n. forms; general (unmarked) dictionary forms preferred; southern (d.s.), Ujarrás (Uj.), San José Cabécar (SJC) and La Estrella (LE) forms used only where no northern/general form was found, and flagged in note. Same conventions as src/content/drafts/cjp.json.
orthography: MMS-TTS cjp (Bible.is CJPTJV) orthography: nasal vowels with combining macron below U+0331, ä ë ö for the extra vowels, ñ, j=/h/, sh, ch, tk, ts, k'. Words attested in the Bible are given in Bible spelling; dictionary-only words keep Margery 1989 spelling (his underline for nasality rendered as U+0331; his acute tone marks kept, though the MMS vocab has no combining acute, so tone on ë/ö is dropped in synthesis). Dictionary spellings were read from the scan images, not the OCR layer; the scan lacks entries 4783–4862 (O section) and the Spanish→Cabécar index for A–O. Entry numbers marked ~ were inferred from neighbouring entries. A reviewer should normalise to one standard (MEP/UCR alphabet, González Campos & Obando 2017) before recording.

sources.title: facebook/mms-tts-cjp model card, vocab.json and tokenizer_config.json (is_uroman=false)
sources.author: Meta AI (Pratap et al., Scaling Speech Technology to 1,000+ Languages)

perro.note: Same in Bible and dictionary. SJC chii (804). In the Bible 'chichi ka̱rbä' (Mt 8:20) means fox, so chichi alone is the dog.
perro.reviewQuestion: ¿'Chichi' es la palabra común para perro?

pez.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 7:10, Mt 13:47, Jn 21:9 'nima' (pez, pescado); margery1989 fish names built on nima, e.g. entry 1782 ják nima 'pez chupapiedras'
pez.note: Bible spelling, used repeatedly for fish. The bare dictionary headword was not located in the scan, only compounds.

venado.source: margery1989 entry 4467 (s. cl. al., zool.) 'venado de montaña', 'venado de cola blanca', 'venado'
venado.note: General (unmarked) form; nasal underlines read from the scan. Not in the NT.

mono.source: margery1989 entry 925 (d.s., s. cl. al.) 'mono' (genérico); //(d.s.) 'mono congo'
mono.note: Southern-dialect generic; no northern generic found, only species: jok 'mono carablanca' (2273), sal 'mono colorado' (araña), pshas 'mono tití'. Chirripó speakers may name a species instead. review: southern-only generic; near-homophone with dukúr/duklö́wö́ cards (see avoidWith).
mono.reviewQuestion: ¿Hay una palabra general para 'mono' en su comunidad, o dicen 'daké̱' / 'jok'?

murcielago.note: General form; variant dakúr (generic, p.46 of scan). Bats can be ill omens in some traditions — check.
murcielago.reviewQuestion: ¿'Dukúr' es el murciélago? ¿Tiene algún mal agüero?

hormiga.note: General form; 3889 ksá wák dolóna 'hormiga negra'. Anthill uses a different stem (tsá wák ju), so no word collision with 'hormiguero'.

abeja.note: General form, read from the scan. Bible Mt 3:4 'bul ñá' = honey, consistent. d.s. mu̱lí̱ 'abeja' // 'colmena' (~4461).
abeja.reviewQuestion: ¿'Búlí ñá̱ wák' es la abeja? ¿Hay una forma más corta?

arana.note: General form; d.n./SJC sárkló (5391). 5352 sálkló batúbatu = black widow.

caracol.source: margery1989 entry ~3220 (s. cl. red., zool.) 'caracol de tierra' (Euglandina spp.)
caracol.note: Land snail as the card requires (never the conch trumpet). Sea snail is dúk. Close in sound to kipö 'hamaca' (hammock card) — check audio distinctness.
caracol.reviewQuestion: ¿'Kipé̱' es el caracol de tierra? ¿Se confunde con 'kipö' (hamaca)?

cangrejo.note: General form; d.s. yawí (7943); sea crab däyë yuwí (d.s.).

armadillo.source: margery1989 entry ~1346 (d.n., s. cl. al., zool.) 'armadillo', 'armado', 'cusuco'
armadillo.note: Northern form; d.s. tsowí (7169), Uj. tsawí. Mild flag: armadillo skin is listed among pieces in healers' bundles (sat k'uö, ~5410); the animal noun itself is everyday.

lagartija.note: General form; variant kirë́kö (3232). ju̱lí̱k also means 'lagartija' but has a second, mythological sense (s., mit.), so it was avoided.

perico.note: General form, names a common parakeet. The generic 'loro' katsö (Uj.) was avoided: near-homonym of the mountain word (ka̱tsä / ká̱ tsö); d.n. katsú is a specific parrot (loro coroniblanco).
perico.reviewQuestion: ¿'Kayö' sirve para un perico verde en general?

raton.note: General form; nasal marks read from the scan. House mouse: kasirí ko̱ñó̱ (d.s., 2858).

gallina.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 23:37 'oshkoro' (gallina), Lk 11:12; margery1989 entry 64 ishkoro (Ch.) 'gallina' (genérico), jóshkoro (d.s.) 'gallinácea', 'gallina'
gallina.note: Bible spelling. Strictly 'chicken'; a hen specifically is óshkoro láki (d.s., 4155 'hembra').

arbol.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 3:10 'kal' (árbol); margery1989 entry 2699 (s. cl. al.) 'árbol' (genérico), 'palo'

hoja.source: margery1989 entry 2986 ká̱ kö́ (s. cl. pl.) 'hoja' (genérico), //(s.) 'maleza'; bibleis-cjptjv spelling ka̱kä (Mt 6:30, Rev 8:7, where it renders 'hierba'); Rev 22:2 'kal kä' (las hojas del árbol)
hoja.note: Bible spelling of the dictionary's generic leaf word. Its second sense is 'weeds/grass', so 'pasto' uses tátsí to avoid a collision. Alternative 'kal kä' = tree leaf (Rev 22:2).
hoja.reviewQuestion: ¿'Ka̱kä' se entiende como hoja (no como hierba)? ¿O es mejor 'kal kä'?

flor.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 6:28 'ka̱ ki̱ka tsitsi wä' (los lirios del campo), Jas 1:10 'ka̱ tsitsiwäí' (la flor de la hierba); margery1989 entry 7099 tsitsía (Ch.) 'flor de planta o de arbusto' (genérico)
flor.note: Northern/Bible form. General dictionary form: má̱ma̱ wö́ (4234, s. cl. red.) 'flor' (genérico). tsitsía also means 'juguete' in d.n.

cacahuate.source: none found in margery1989 (searched 'maní', 'cacahuate', Arachis) or Bible.is CJPTJV
cacahuate.note: No entry. The dictionary 'manú' is a tree (Minquartia), not peanut. Left null.

raiz.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 13:6 'ka irä ñak kicha ta' (no tenía raíz); margery1989 entry 3183 kicha, third sense 'raíz' (must be preceded by the plant term), 1533 gicha 'raíz' (genérico)
raiz.note: Bible phrase. kicha alone is 'rope' (the cuerda card) — the dictionary says the 'root' sense needs a preceding term, which ñak ('base, foot of a plant', cf. Mt 3:10 'kal ñak') supplies.

calabaza.note: No squash entry found. Related words name different plants: jär wö 'chayote' (1857), mö / tká̱ 'calabazo, jícaro' (gourd tree and vessel, used for the jícara card). The Spanish A–O index is missing from the scan, so an 'ayote' entry could be missed. Left null.

yuca.note: General form. SJC alí (39). One syllable.

camote.source: margery1989 entry 141 (Uj., s. cl. red.) 'camote'; //(Uj.) 'papa chiricana'
camote.note: Ujarrás only; the same word also names 'papa chiricana' (another tuber). No northern form found.

guayaba.note: The entry names the tree (fruit is edible per the entry); no separate fruit form found. Nasal mark read from the scan. SJC shölí / shuno.

algodon.source: margery1989 entry ~6332 (s., bot.) 'algodón'; //(adj.) 'de color blanco intenso'

huevo.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 11:12 'oshkoro si̱a' (huevo); margery1989 entry ~5637 si̱a̱ 'huevo de ave' (must be preceded by the species, e.g. óshkoro si̱a̱ 'huevo de gallinácea')
huevo.note: Bible phrase; si̱a̱ cannot stand alone for 'egg'. SENSITIVE: the first sense of the same dictionary entry is the small stones the suquias (healers) carry in a bag for ceremonies; the full phrase 'oshkoro si̱a' avoids that reading but reviewers should confirm.
huevo.reviewQuestion: ¿'Oshkoro si̱a' (huevo de gallina) está bien para la carta? ¿'Si̱a' solo tiene un sentido sagrado?

hongo.note: Northern form; 6251 shotorói needs íshökö ('ground') or kal ('tree') before it; SJC jotorró. No ritual-mushroom sense found in the sources; card shows an edible cap.

platano.source: margery1989 entry 835 (s. cl. al., bot.) 'fruto de musácea' (genérico), 'banano' (genérico)
platano.note: General form. Plantain (Musa paradisiaca) is tsalá (6928), which also means 'res' (cattle) in family speech. The dictionary also lists a family-speech use of chimo̱ for the pig.

pasto.note: General form. The Bible uses ka̱kä for 'hierba' (Mt 6:30), but that word is the leaf card, so tátsí avoids a collision. tala (d.n., p.u.) also 'zacate' but is the thunder word.

papaya.note: General form; d.n. k'ichö (~3377); SJC gochö (1543).

fuego.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 3:10, Rev 8:7, Jn 18:18 'yökö' (fuego); margery1989 entry 8091 yökö 'fuego', 'fogón', 'fogata'

humo.note: Bible form; Rev 9:2 also has shka̱la̱, so -i may be a suffix. Dictionary 'humo' entries (~6130, ~6206) are legible only in OCR, not verified. review: -i suffix unresolved.

neblina.note: Northern form; d.s. mo̱ chaka (~4372). Built on mo̱ 'cloud' (nube card), so the two cards share a syllable. Bible Jas 4:14 renders 'neblina' with mo̱ alone.

granizo.source: bibleis-cjptjv Rev 16:21 'ka̱li̱ kole' (granizo); Rev 8:7, Rev 11:19 'ka̱li̱ wäkole'
granizo.note: Bible phrase built on ka̱li̱ 'rain' (lluvia card). A d.s. dictionary entry for 'granizo' (5701) was seen only in OCR, not verified.

nieve.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 28:3 'suruu si̱ nieve käi' (blanco como la nieve), Rev 1:14 'nieve käi'
nieve.note: Spanish loan used inside the Cabécar text; no native term in margery1989. Snow does not occur in Talamanca.

hielo.source: none found in margery1989 or Bible.is CJPTJV
hielo.note: No entry and no NT occurrence. Left null.

amanecer.source: bibleis-cjptjv Jn 21:4 'ka̱ñir dawa̱ kja ra' (al amanecer); margery1989 entry ~3844 kó̱ñí̱r dawa (d.s., s.) 'amanecer', 'madrugada'
amanecer.note: Bible spelling of the dictionary noun. Verb 'it dawned': ka̱ñinawa̱ (Acts 27:39).

noche.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 2:8, Jn 3:2, Rev 14:11 'tuina' (noche); margery1989 tuwina (s. cl. pl.) 'noche', //(adj.) 'oscuro(a)' (~6754)
noche.note: Bible spelling; dictionary tuwina. Also used adverbially ('at night').

cielo.note: Northern form; d.s. ká̱ jöí (2963). SENSITIVE: the Bible's word is ka̱jöir (sky in Mt 16:2-3, but also 'heaven', Mt 3:16, Mt 6:9); the plain dictionary word avoids the religious sense.
cielo.reviewQuestion: ¿'Ká̱ ktö' para el cielo? ¿O dicen 'ka̱jöir'? ¿Alguna tiene sentido religioso?

sombra.source: margery1989 Spanish index s.v. 'sombra': olói (4815); entry 4815 is on pages missing from the scan. bibleis-cjptjv Acts 5:15 'ioloi(bä)' (su sombra)
sombra.note: The entry itself could not be read (scan lacks entries 4783–4862). The Bible uses oloi for 'shadow' (Acts 5:15, Mt 4:16) but 'ka̱ oloi' for 'light' (Mt 4:16, 17:2). SJC diö́köl (1214) also means 'drawing, photo'. SENSITIVE: in many Talamancan traditions the shadow is tied to the soul — check. review: attested only via Spanish index (olói 4815, entry unread) plus Bible oloi; kept low. Do not record as high until the entry or a speaker confirms; soul-related sense unchecked.
sombra.reviewQuestion: ¿'Olói' es la sombra? ¿Tiene un sentido espiritual (alma)?

rocio.note: General form; also mo̱ riö (s.) 'rocío' and ka̱li̱ pöi (d.s.).

remolino.source: margery1989 entry ~7811 wö́shkiri (s.) 'remolino' (must be preceded by díglö 'agua' or si̱wá (d.s.) ~ si̱má (d.n.) 'viento')
remolino.note: The dictionary gives wö́shkiri with the rule that it is preceded by 'wind' or 'water'; the full phrase is assembled per that rule (wind in Bible spelling si̱wa̱), not printed as a phrase. With díglö it means a water eddy. SENSITIVE: si̱wa̱ also means traditional knowledge (see viento card); whirlwinds may be read as spirits.
remolino.reviewQuestion: ¿'Si̱wa̱ wöshkiri' se dice para un remolino de viento? ¿Tiene algún sentido delicado?

agua.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 3:16, Jn 4:6, Jn 2:6 'diklä' (agua); margery1989 díglö / díklö (s.) 'agua', //(s. cl. al.) 'río' (~1098, ~1160)
agua.note: Bible spelling (dictionary díglö). WORD COLLISION: the same word is the river (rio card); per selection rule 8 only one of the two can stay.
agua.reviewQuestion: ¿'Diklä' para el agua? ¿Hay otra palabra para distinguir río?

ceniza.note: Bible spelling; dictionary mu̱lí̱tö. Embers: mu̱lí̱tö bär ta (d.s.).

trueno.source: bibleis-cjptjv Rev 4:5, Rev 11:19 'tala bula…' (truenos); margery1989 entry ~6449 tala (s.) 'trueno'
trueno.note: SENSITIVE: the next entry is Tala (n.p., mit.) 'el espíritu del trueno'. tala also means 'potrero' and (p.u.) 'zacate' in d.n. review: text 'tala' withdrawn. 'tala' is also the name of the thunder spirit (Tala, n.p., mit.); excluded from the children's game pending community consent.
trueno.reviewQuestion: ¿Se puede usar 'tala' para trueno en un juego infantil, o hay otra palabra?

rio.source: bibleis-cjptjv Acts 16:13 'diklä kjäka' (junto al río), Rev 22:1; margery1989 díklö (1160), díglö (1098) 'río' (Spanish index)
rio.note: WORD COLLISION with the agua card (same word). Uj. díglö kayege (p.u.) 'río' is rare. Per rule 8 only one of agua/rio can stay. review: text 'diklä' withdrawn. Identical to agua (diklä); agua kept, since Bible attests diklä as plain water and 'diklä kjäka' (by the water) is not a distinct river noun.
rio.reviewQuestion: ¿Hay una palabra distinta para 'río' (quebrada/río grande) o solo 'diklä'?

lago.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 5:1 'Genesaret tipei' (lago de Genesaret), Lk 8:22-23 'tipä'; margery1989 entry 6566 tipö́ (s. cl. red.) 'lago', 'laguna'; //'pozo'
lago.note: Bible spelling (dictionary tipö́). The dictionary's second sense 'pozo' is why the pozo card uses a different phrase.

piedra.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 7:9, Mt 7:25 'jak' (piedra, roca); margery1989 entry ~1777 ják (s. cl. red.) 'piedra'
piedra.note: Plain stone; the healers' sacred stones are a different word (si̱a̱). Note jak also 'robo' (homonym).

arena.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 7:26, Heb 11:12 'ksa̱' (arena); margery1989 entry ~3892 ksá (s.) 'arena'
arena.note: Bible spelling. Near-homograph of ksa 'rope, vine, bridge' (puente card) — only nasality/tone differ.

playa.source: bibleis-cjptjv Acts 21:5 'däyë kse̱i ki̱' (en la playa), Heb 11:12 (orilla del mar)
playa.note: Bible phrase ('edge of the sea'); lake shore is tipä kse̱i (Mt 13:2). Dictionary has only SJC forms ak ulaitö (19), tsailitö (6975).

cascada.note: La Estrella dialect only; no northern form found.

charco.source: none found in margery1989 or Bible.is CJPTJV
charco.note: No word for 'charco'. Closest are 'poza' words (tipö́, dapä SJC), which name river pools and collide with the lake word. Left null.

lodo.source: margery1989 entry ~1289 (d.n., s.) 'barro', 'lodo'; bibleis-cjptjv Jn 9:6 'dölií wà' (con el lodo)
lodo.note: Northern form, matches the Bible. General dö̱ (1278) is too short.

barranca.note: Northern form; d.n. kä̱yöna 'barranco' // 'derrumbe' also exists. review: 'ítt'ö' has a doubled consonant plus apostrophe, atypical for the orthography; possible scan misreading, entry number only approximate.

llano.note: Northern form for savanna, not exactly 'plain'. General sák (5784) 'sabana'; SJC ká̱ jké̱i (2962) 'terreno plano'. review: k'á̱ kötö is near-homophone of cielo ká̱ ktö́; sabana is not the same as plain.
llano.reviewQuestion: ¿Cómo dicen un 'llano' o terreno plano: 'k'á̱ kötö', 'sák'?

ola.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 8:24 'tjuäke̱' (las olas), Lk 8:24 'tipä tjuäke̱', Jas 1:6 'däyë tjuäke̱' (la ola del mar); margery1989 entry 6605 t'uö́ (d.n.) 'ola', 'onda'
ola.note: Bible spelling; may be a plural/collective form. Sea wave also däyë t'uö (d.n.).

concha.source: margery1989 entry ~5235 (d.n., s.) 'concha' (genérico); //(d.n.) 'small land or sea snail'
concha.note: Northern form; second sense overlaps the caracol card. Other: yöksoró 'concha de caracol', ksa (d.s.) 'concha' (homograph of rope).

valle.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 3:5 'ka̱ dochoi biköle' (todo valle); cf. Jn 18:1 'diklä dochoi' (torrente); margery1989 díglö dochoi (d.s., 1102) 'quebrada pequeña'
valle.note: Bible rendering of 'valle'; dochoi seems to mean a hollow or ravine, so it may overlap 'barranca'. No dictionary entry for 'valle' (index has only a place name).

tierra.source: bibleis-cjptjv Jn 9:6 'ishäkä ki̱' (en tierra), Rev 8:7; margery1989 íshökö (d.n., s.) 'tierra', 'suelo' (~1700)
tierra.note: Bible spelling of the dictionary word. Mild flag: earth is one of the four elements named in a cosmological list (p.351 of scan); the card shows plain soil.

hacha.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 3:10 'bak' (el hacha); margery1989 entry 154 bak (s. cl. pl.) 'hacha'
hacha.note: Homonyms: (d.n.) 'espalda', (SJC) 'tambor'. The tambor card is sábák, which contains bak.

red.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 4:18, Mt 13:47 'kla' (red); margery1989 entry 3478 kla (SJC) 'red', 'telaraña'
red.note: Bible fishing-net word. SJC also uses kla for spider web, so the telaraña card uses another word.

cuerda.source: margery1989 entry 3183 kicha (s. cl. al.) 'soga', 'cuerda', 'mecate'; bibleis-cjptjv Acts 27:40 'ko̱no wäkukäklä kicha' (las amarras del timón)
cuerda.note: General form. Shared by the hilo card ('tulúk kicha') and the raiz card ('ñak kicha'). ksa (3876) is also 'soga' but is the puente card word (Bible Jn 2:15 'ksa' cords).

jicara.note: General form; mö 'calabazo, jícaro' names the gourd tree and vessel. SENSITIVE: gourd bowls serve chicha in ceremonies; card must show an everyday bowl. One syllable.
jicara.reviewQuestion: ¿'Tká̱' es el guacal/jícara? ¿Tiene uso ceremonial que evitar?

metate.reviewQuestion: ¿'Jáj kuö' es la piedra de moler?

comal.source: none found in margery1989 or Bible.is CJPTJV
comal.note: No entry for comal or toasting pan. Left null.

escoba.note: Southern only; also ká̱ sigöglö (d.s.). SJC verb ush kalö 'barrer'.

aguja.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 19:24 'tuluk wä' (el ojo de la aguja); margery1989 entry ~6731 tulúk (s. cl. pl.) 'aguja'
aguja.note: Bible spelling (dictionary tulúk). Also the first word of the hilo card ('tulúk kicha').

banco.note: General form; d.n. ñäk ata miklö (4667). No ceremonial-stool sense noted in the entry.
banco.reviewQuestion: ¿'Ñákglö' es el banco/banquito? ¿Hay bancos ceremoniales con otro nombre?

sombrero.note: Northern form; d.n. tsá̱ú̱ kí̱ tkëna (~7029); d.s. ká̱lbá (~3002).

morral.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 10:4 'däli tsa̱klä' (alforja); margery1989 entry ~976 dalí tsáklö (d.n., s. cl. pl.) 'bolso de mano'
morral.note: Bible spelling of the dictionary's d.n. word. The cesto card bójkö also means 'bolso pequeño'; dalí is also in the tienda card ('dalí wí').

hamaca.note: General form; SJC gopo (1548). Close in sound to kipé̱ 'land snail' (caracol card).

petate.note: No entry ('tapesco' entries are raised platforms, not mats). Left null.

camino.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 7:13-14, Lk 8:5 'ña̱la̱' (camino); margery1989 entry 4691 ña̱la̱ (s. cl. pl.) 'camino', 'sendero'

pozo.source: bibleis-cjptjv Jn 4:6 'Jacob wa̱ diklä talanaklä' (el pozo de Jacob), Jn 4:12
pozo.note: Bible phrase ('place to draw water'). Dictionary 'pozo' words collide with other cards: tipö́ (lago) and díglö tsi̱ní̱ (d.n., 'pozo, noria' and 'manantial', the manantial card). Card must not show a cenote.

nido.source: margery1989 entry ~1349 (s. cl. pl.) 'nido de ave'; bibleis-cjptjv Mt 8:20, Lk 9:58 'du … ju' (las aves … nidos)
nido.note: Literally 'bird house' (du 'bird', ju 'house', the casa card).

colmena.note: Southern form; d.s. mu̱lí̱ also 'abeja' // 'colmena'. SJC bulu (695) 'colmena' is avoided: homonym of bulu (696, mit.) 'espíritu'.

hormiguero.note: General form; d.s. tsá wák ju̱, SJC tsá wá wí. Different stem from the ant word (ksá wák), so no direct collision.

telarana.source: margery1989 entry 6097 (d.s., s. cl. pl.) 'telaraña' (also 'tira de bejuco', 'astilla')
telarana.note: Southern; primary senses are 'vine strip' and 'splinter'. SJC kla = red (net card).

patio.gloss: house yard, ground around a house
patio.source: margery1989 entry 2394 (d.s., s.) 'terreno inmediato que rodea una casa'; //(d.s.) 'patio de una casa'
patio.note: Southern form. The Bible's 'ijuitä' (Lk 13:19) renders 'huerto', so patio and huerto may share a word in speech.

huerto.note: Bible phrase for 'huerto' (Gethsemane); literally a place of trees/plants, i.e. a grove rather than a vegetable plot. Lk 13:19 uses 'ijuitä' (his garden). No dictionary entry found.

cerca.note: Northern form; possibly an old loan from Spanish 'cerca' — reviewer to judge. Visually confusable with corral. review: dictionary primary senses are 'muralla/pared'; 'cerca' appears only as a //sub-sense, and sérka looks like a Spanish loan, so kind may need to be 'loan'; confidence lowered.

puerta.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 7:7, Lk 13:25 'ju kjä' (puerta); margery1989 entry 2407 ju k'ö (d.n., s. cl. pl.) 'puerta'
puerta.note: Bible spelling of the d.n. dictionary form.

techo.note: Bible phrase. Dictionary: shpéi (d.n., 6306, after ju), ju k'ö tkële (d.n., 2406), ju bata (d.s.).

escalera.note: Southern; also klö́ gata (d.s., 3528). kal = wood, fitting a notched-log ladder.

troje.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 12:18 'däli bläklä jui' (graneros); Mt 3:12, Mt 6:26 'ibläklä jui'
troje.note: Bible phrase ('house for keeping things'); Jn 2:6 uses 'diklä bläklä jui' for water jars, so the core means 'storage container'. No dictionary entry.
troje.reviewQuestion: ¿Guardan el maíz en un troje/tapesco? ¿Cómo lo llaman?

cocina.source: margery1989 entry ~8098 (d.s., s.) 'cocina', 'lugar de la casa destinado a la cocina'

corral.source: none found in margery1989; Bible.is Jn 10:1 has only a verb phrase ('oveja kjätkeleksa̱', where sheep are enclosed)
corral.note: No noun found; the Bible phrase is sheep-specific and clause-like. Left null.

gusano.source: margery1989 entry ~810 (d.n., s. cl. al.) 'gusano' (genérico); bibleis-cjptjv Mk 9:48 'chichöñaí' (su gusano)
gusano.note: Northern form. General í (s. cl. al.) 'gusano' is a single vowel, too short.

zorro.note: Bible term (lit. a kind of wild dog). Dictionary 'zorro' entries are opossums (bakalí 'zorro pelón', 159), a different animal.
zorro.reviewQuestion: ¿'Chichi ka̱rbä' es el zorro (no la zarigüeya)?

pato.note: Northern form ('lake people'); d.s. duwák (1405), tögölo, toklo. review: spelling inconsistent with lago (tipä Bible / tipö́ dictionary): tip'ö́ has an apostrophe and different vowel; normalise with the lago card before recording.

luciernaga.source: margery1989 entry 8186 (d.n., s. cl. pl., ent.) 'luciérnaga'
luciernaga.note: Northern form; d.s. kutu, SJC tkowä, d.s. dowá wák (1310).

cantaro.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mk 14:13 'u̱ yaka wí̱' (cántaro de agua), Jn 4:28 'u̱yaka wí̱' (cántaro); margery1989 entry 7374 u̱ 'olla'
cantaro.note: Bible phrase. Close to the olla card (ká̱ wí̱).

pelota.source: none found in margery1989 or Bible.is CJPTJV

collar.note: Northern form. SENSITIVE: siwá (SJC, 5631) is the collar the suquia wears in ceremonies — avoided. Others: sówí wö (Uj.), ksöwí wö (d.s.).
collar.reviewQuestion: ¿'Kulí mu̱a̱glö' es un collar común (no ceremonial)?

cuchara.note: Northern form; 7453 'cucharita'. wá ñá na (d.n., 7493) is 'eating utensil, plate, spoon'.

remo.note: General form; d.s. ko̱no̱ kalí and other kono- compounds.

sal.note: WORD COLLISION with the existing mar card (same word); per rule 8 this card cannot coexist with mar. review: text 'däyë' withdrawn. Identical to existing mar card (däyë); mar kept in the deck, sal marked missing until a distinct salt word is confirmed.

semilla.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 8:5 'idäli wä' (su semilla), Lk 8:11 'däli wä' (la semilla)
semilla.note: Bible phrase (everyday seed). SENSITIVE: the dictionary generic ditsö́ (1235) also means 'clan', and the seed (ditsö) is central to the Talamancan creation narrative (people created from seeds) — avoided for that reason.
semilla.reviewQuestion: ¿'Däli wä' para la semilla? ¿Usar 'ditsö' sería delicado?

lena.note: Northern form; LE yökö́ ták; d.s. chakö / chkö láglö (855). Bible Acts 28:3 'yökö batala' (sticks for the fire).
